s: Which Vice-President, besides S. Radhakrishnan, served two full terms?
x: Hamid Ansari served two full terms as Vice-President from 2007 to 2017. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the other Vice-President associated with two terms.

s: Who was the first President of India to die in office?
x: Dr Zakir Husain was the first President to die in office; V.V. Giri then acted as President in 1969.

s: Who is the Vice-President of India elected after the mid-term vacancy created by the resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar in July 2025?
x: C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected Vice-President after the mid-term vacancy caused by Jagdeep Dhankhar’s resignation in July 2025.

s: Which future Vice-President had earlier been India's Ambassador to the USSR?
x: S. Radhakrishnan was Ambassador to the USSR (1949–52) before becoming the first VP; V.V. Giri served in Sri Lanka and K.R. Narayanan in China.

s: During which period did M. Venkaiah Naidu of Andhra Pradesh serve as Vice-President?
x: M. Venkaiah Naidu (Nellore) was Vice-President from 2017 to 2022.

s: Who is the present Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
x: The Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected Vice-President in September 2025.

s: Who among the following became President of India after serving as Vice-President?
x: Radhakrishnan, Zakir Husain and V.V. Giri moved from Vice-President to President; Neelam Sanjiva Reddy became President without being VP.

s: Who acted as President of India after Dr. Zakir Husain died in office in 1969?
x: Zakir Husain was the first President to die in office; Vice-President V.V. Giri then acted as President.

s: From which constituency did P.V. Narasimha Rao, who became Prime Minister in 1991 without being an MP, later enter the Lok Sabha?
x: Narasimha Rao, the first PM from South India, entered the Lok Sabha from Nandyal.

s: Who was the first Prime Minister of India and also holds the record for the longest overall tenure as Prime Minister?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and had the maximum aggregate tenure as Prime Minister, from 1947 to 1964.

s: Who was the first acting Prime Minister of India (in 1964 and 1966)?
x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first acting Prime Minister, in 1964 and again in 1966.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a Prime Minister of India who came from the Rajya Sabha?
x: The Prime Ministers from the Rajya Sabha were Indira Gandhi (the first, 1966), H.D. Deve Gowda, I.K. Gujral and Manmohan Singh. Charan Singh was a Lok Sabha member, not a Rajya Sabha PM (he is noted as the PM who never faced the Lok Sabha).

s: Who was the first non-Congress Prime Minister of India?
x: Morarji Desai was the first non-Congress Prime Minister of India.

s: Which Prime Minister had the shortest tenure, 13 days in 1996?
x: A.B. Vajpayee's 1996 tenure of 13 days is the shortest; Nanda was acting PM and Charan Singh never faced the Lok Sabha.

s: Who was the first Prime Minister of India from South India?
x: P.V. Narasimha Rao became PM in 1991 without being an MP and was the first PM from South India.

s:
Arrange the following Prime Ministers of India in chronological order:
1. Morarji Desai
2. Lal Bahadur Shastri
3. Chandra Shekhar
4. Charan Singh
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Shastri (1964-66) came first, then Morarji Desai (1977-79), Charan Singh (1979-80) and Chandra Shekhar (1990-91).

s: Who was the first Prime Minister of India to be a member of the Rajya Sabha?
x: Indira Gandhi was a Rajya Sabha member when she became Prime Minister in 1966 - the first PM from the Rajya Sabha.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Indira Gandhi was the first woman Prime Minister of India.
2. Indira Gandhi was the first Prime Minister from the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Indira Gandhi (1966) was both the first woman PM and the first PM who was a Rajya Sabha member.

s: In July 2025, Narendra Modi's continuous tenure as Prime Minister went past that of which Prime Minister?
x: In July 2025 Modi passed Indira Gandhi's continuous tenure; Nehru still holds the record.

s: Who among the following form the electoral college that elects the Vice-President of India?
o: elected members of both Houses of Parliament only
elected MPs and elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
all members of both Houses of Parliament, elected and nominated
all MPs and elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
x: All MPs, elected and nominated, vote by PR-STV and secret ballot; State legislatures have no role in the Vice-President's election.

s: The 39th Constitutional Amendment and the 44th Constitutional Amendment had what effect on Presidential election disputes?
o: The 39th Amendment vested the disputes in Parliament and the 44th retained that arrangement
The 39th Amendment removed the Supreme Court’s power and the 44th Amendment restored it
The 39th Amendment created the power and the 44th Amendment abolished it
Both Amendments transferred the power to the Election Commission
x: The 39th Amendment of 1975 took away the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction over these disputes, while the 44th Amendment of 1978 restored it.

s: Which Article makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
x: Article 64 makes the Vice-President ex-officio Chairman; 63 creates the office, 66 covers election and 67 the term.

s: On which office is the office of the Vice-President of India modelled?
o: Deputy Prime Minister of the UK
x: The Indian Vice-President's office is modelled on the American Vice-President.

s: The Vice-President of India is ex officio President of which of the following bodies?
x: The Vice-President is also the ex-officio President of the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA).

s: When both Houses are full, the electoral college for the Vice-President has how many members?
x: All 788 MPs, elected and nominated, elect the Vice-President; State Legislatures have no role.

s: Who decides disputes regarding the election of the Vice-President?
x: Under Article 71 all disputes over the Vice-President's election are decided finally by the Supreme Court.

s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Parliament of India under Article 79?
x: Article 79: Parliament = President + Council of States + House of the People; the VP chairs the RS but is not a member or part of Parliament.

s: By which system is the Vice-President of India elected?
o: First-past-the-post system by members of the Lok Sabha
Proportional representation by single transferable vote, by secret ballot
Open ballot by simple majority of both Houses
x: The Vice-President is elected by MPs of both Houses through PR-STV, and voting is by secret ballot.

s: Under which Act are the elections to the offices of President and Vice-President of India held?
x: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs these elections.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India?
x: Article 63 creates the office of Vice-President; Article 64 makes him ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a qualification for election as Vice-President of India?
o: Qualification for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
Qualification for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha
x: The Vice-President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old and qualified for election to the Rajya Sabha. Qualification for election to the Lok Sabha is not the prescribed condition.

s: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
x: Sardar Patel was the first Deputy PM; the office is not mentioned in the Constitution and its holder takes oath as an ordinary Minister.

s: When Manmohan Singh, a Rajya Sabha member, was Prime Minister, who was named Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha?
x: The Leader of the House is not a constitutional office; a PM who is not a Lok Sabha member nominates a minister, and Pranab Mukherjee was named under Manmohan Singh.

s: Which body is the core decision-making body of the Union Government?
x: The Union Cabinet, the top tier of the ministerial hierarchy, is the core decision-making body, not the whole Council of Ministers.

s: On what is the classification of Union Ministers into different ranks based?
o: convention and the choice of the Prime Minister
the Third Schedule of the Constitution
x: The Constitution does not classify ministers into ranks; the ranks, including Deputy Minister, rest on convention and the PM's choice.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the categories of Union Ministers?
o: A Deputy Minister heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.
A Cabinet Minister heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.
A Minister of State with independent charge holds a ministry on his or her own.
A Minister of State is attached to a Cabinet Minister.
x: A Deputy Minister only assists a senior Minister; it is the Cabinet Minister who heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.

s: What proportion of Andhra and Telangana representation in the united Andhra Pradesh cabinet did the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement provide?
x: The 1956 Gentlemen’s Agreement fixed the united Andhra Pradesh cabinet proportion at 60% Andhra and 40% Telangana.

s: The word referring to the Union Cabinet was inserted into Article 352(3) by which amendment?
x: The word 'Cabinet' was absent from the original Constitution and was inserted into Article 352(3) by the 44th Amendment (1978), requiring the Cabinet's written advice for an Emergency.

s: What is the Prime Minister's Office?
o: parliamentary committee of the Lok Sabha
statutory body headed by the President
extra-constitutional staff agency of the Prime Minister
x: The Prime Minister’s Office is not mentioned in the Constitution; it is an extra-constitutional staff agency assisting the Prime Minister.

s: What are Ministers who head their own ministry without Cabinet rank called?
o: Ministers of State attached to Cabinet Ministers
x: Ministers of State with independent charge hold their own ministry; Deputy Ministers only assist and Cabinet Ministers have Cabinet rank.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Prime Minister:
1. The post is not mentioned in the Constitution.
2. He takes the oath as an ordinary Minister.
3. He enjoys the powers of the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Deputy PM is not a constitutional post and is sworn in as an ordinary Minister; he has no PM powers, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tie in the Rajya Sabha – Vice-President has no vote
Resolution for his own removal – Vice-President presides
Re-election of the Vice-President – any number of times
Vote of the Vice-President – on every motion in the first instance
x: The Vice-President can be re-elected any number of times. He has only a casting vote in a tie and does not preside while his own removal is considered.

s: Who administers the oath of office to the Vice-President of India?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most judge of the Supreme Court
x: Under Article 69 the President administers the Vice-President's oath; the CJI administers the President's oath.

s: While the Vice-President acts as President, who presides over the Rajya Sabha?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: While acting as President under Article 65, the Vice-President stops doing the duties of Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and the Deputy Chairman presides.

s: To whom does the Vice-President of India address his resignation?
x: Under Article 67(a) the Vice-President resigns by writing to the President, and the resignation takes effect immediately. The President resigns to the Vice-President; the CJI administers the President's oath; the Speaker is informed of the President's resignation; the Prime Minister receives no constitutional resignation of either office.

s: Within what time must a vacancy in the office of the Vice-President of India be filled?
o: Within six months of the vacancy in every case
As soon as possible, without a constitutionally prescribed six-month deadline
Within one year, after approval by the Supreme Court
Only at the next general election to the Lok Sabha
x: Article 68 requires an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President as soon as possible. Unlike the vacancy in the office of President, no six-month deadline is prescribed for this election.

s: What is the maximum period for which the Vice-President may act as President when the office of President falls vacant or the President is unable to discharge functions?
x: The Vice-President can act as President for at most six months, within which a new President must be elected.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the removal of the Vice-President of India?
o: The resolution must originate in the Rajya Sabha.
The resolution needs a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha.
The Lok Sabha must agree to the resolution by a simple majority.
The Constitution specifies the grounds for removal.
x: The Constitution does not state any grounds for removing the Vice-President; the other three statements describe the procedure correctly.

s: What is the minimum notice required before a resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be moved?
x: The removal resolution needs 14 days' notice, is moved only in the Rajya Sabha and must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

s: Whose salary and allowances does the Vice-President draw while acting as President?
o: Those of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: While acting as President, the VP stops doing the Chairman's work and draws the President's salary, not the Chairman's.

s: On the resignation of the President, whom must the Vice-President inform immediately under Article 56(2)?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: Article 56(2) requires the Vice-President to communicate the President's resignation at once to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

s: Which of the following is correct about the tenure of the Prime Minister?
o: The Prime Minister can be removed only by the Supreme Court.
The Prime Minister holds office for life unless removed by impeachment.
The Prime Minister continues in office while commanding the confidence of the Lok Sabha, subject to the President's pleasure in the constitutional sense.
The Prime Minister has a fixed tenure of five years irrespective of legislative support.
x: The Prime Minister has no fixed tenure and ordinarily continues while enjoying the confidence of the Lok Sabha. The Constitution formally states that Ministers hold office during the President's pleasure.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Prime Minister is correctly matched?
o: Oath of the PM – administered by the Chief Justice of India
Membership at appointment – must be a Lok Sabha member
A non-member PM – must enter Parliament within one year
x: The President appoints the PM under Article 75(1) and administers his oath. The PM may belong to either House, and a non-member gets six months to become an MP.

s: Unlike the UK Prime Minister, who must belong to the House of Commons, to which House may the Indian Prime Minister belong?
x: The UK Prime Minister must be in the House of Commons, while the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.

s: On whose advice does the President appoint the other Union Ministers?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: The PM advises the President on appointing Ministers and on dissolving the Lok Sabha; the CJI is appointed through the collegium process, not on the PM's advice.

s: Who among the following can ask any Union Minister to resign?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: As head of the Council of Ministers, the Prime Minister selects Ministers, allocates portfolios and can ask any Minister to resign.

s: P.V. Narasimha Rao became Prime Minister in 1991 without being a Member of Parliament. Within what period did he have to become a member of either House?
x: Under Article 75(5) a non-member PM or Minister must become an MP within six consecutive months.

s: Which of the following is NOT a duty of the Prime Minister under Article 78?
o: Furnishing information relating to administration when called for by the President
Submitting for the consideration of the Council any matter decided by an individual Minister when the President requires it
Communicating to the President decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals
Administering the oath of office and secrecy to all Union Ministers
x: Options A, B and C are duties of the Prime Minister under Article 78 (communicating Council decisions, furnishing information, and placing a minister's individual decision before the Council when the President requires). Administering the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers is done by the President, not the PM.

s: Which Article provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President?
x: Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise; Article 75 covers appointment and tenure, and Article 78 the PM's duties.

s: What is the position of the President of India regarding ministerial advice during a National Emergency?
o: acquires unrestricted discretion to disregard the advice of the Council of Ministers
continues to be bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers
becomes the real executive in place of the Prime Minister
may dismiss the entire Council without following constitutional advice
x: A National Emergency does not confer discretionary power on the President to disregard the binding advice of the Council of Ministers. The parliamentary executive relationship continues.

s: Which Article lays down the duties of the Prime Minister towards the President?
x: The PM's duties to communicate decisions and furnish information to the President are in Article 78; Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise.

s: Under Article 74(1), the advice of the Council of Ministers becomes binding on the President after he does which of the following?
o: secures approval from the Election Commission
refers the matter to the Supreme Court
obtains the consent of the Rajya Sabha
x: The President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice once, but must act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration.

s: Which Article provides that the advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into by any court?
x: Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice; Article 77 deals with action in the President's name, authentication of orders and business rules.

s: Under Article 77(3), the President makes rules for the convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India and for its allocation among Ministers. What are these rules called?
o: Union Executive Rules and Ministerial Responsibility Rules
Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules
Conduct of Government Rules and Delegation Rules
Rules of Procedure of Parliament and Cabinet Manual
x: Article 77(3) is implemented through the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961 and the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961.

s: In which year were the Allocation of Business Rules and the Transaction of Business Rules made under Article 77(3)?
x: Both sets of Rules were made in 1961 under Article 77(3); the President allocates portfolios on the PM's advice.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 74?
o: Article 74(1) provides a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
The President may ask for reconsideration of advice once
Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice
Article 74(3) lays down the duties of the Prime Minister
x: Article 74(3) does not exist; the PM's duties to the President are in Article 78.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution is all executive action of the Government of India expressed to be taken in the name of the President?
x: Article 77(1) says all executive action of the Government of India shall be taken in the name of the President.

s: Under the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, the President may return the advice of the Council of Ministers for reconsideration:
x: The 44th Amendment lets the President return ministerial advice once for reconsideration; the advice binds after that.

s: Under the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025, on which day would a Minister detained for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five or more years be removed?
x: The Bill provides for removal on the 31st day after 30 consecutive days of detention; it touches Articles 75, 164 and 239AA.

s: Under Article 164(1A), what is the maximum number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a 294-member Assembly?
x: 15% of 294 is 44.1, so the maximum is 44 (e.g. West Bengal), not 45.

s: With a Lok Sabha of 543 members, what is the maximum number of Ministers, including the PM, in the Union Council of Ministers?
x: Article 75(1A) caps Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha's strength: 15% of 543 gives a maximum of 81.

s: What did the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 provide?
o: The Council of Ministers, including the PM, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
The President may return ministerial advice once for reconsideration
Reservation of one-third seats for women in the Lok Sabha
x: The 91st Amendment (2003) inserted Article 75(1A) capping the Union ministry at 15% of the Lok Sabha; the 97th dealt with co-operatives.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:
1. The 15% limit on the Union Council of Ministers includes the Prime Minister.
2. In a State, the number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not be less than 12.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 75(1A) counts the PM within the 15% cap, and Article 164(1A) sets a minimum of 12 Ministers in a State.

s: Which Article of the Constitution fixes the 15% limit and the minimum of 12 on the size of a State Council of Ministers?
x: Article 164(1A), added by the 91st Amendment, applies the 15% cap to States with a floor of 12 Ministers.

s: Which Articles of the Constitution does the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 touch?
x: The Bill, on removing a PM/CM/Minister detained for 30 days, touches Articles 75 (Union), 164 (States) and 239AA (Delhi).

s: Who chairs the Inter-State Council?
x: The Prime Minister chairs the Inter-State Council, as well as NITI Aayog, the National Development Council and the National Integration Council.

s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
x: The PM was ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission; its first Deputy Chairman, of Cabinet rank, was Gulzarilal Nanda.

s: Who is the Chairman of NITI Aayog?
x: The Prime Minister chairs NITI Aayog, as he chairs the Inter-State Council and the National Development Council.

s: Who among the following is NOT a member of the jury for the Gandhi Peace Prize?
o: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
x: The five-member jury of the Gandhi Peace Prize (started 1995) includes the PM, the CJI and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, not the President.

s: Under which Act was the National Disaster Management Authority, chaired by the Prime Minister, set up?
x: The NDMA, headed by the Prime Minister, was set up under the Disaster Management Act of 23 December 2005.

s: In which year was the Gandhi Peace Prize instituted?
x: The Gandhi Peace Prize was started in 1995, Gandhi's 125th birth anniversary year.

s: What does Article 75(1B) provide for a Member of Parliament disqualified for defection under the Tenth Schedule?
o: eligible only after approval by the Election Commission
permanently barred from becoming a Union Minister
ineligible to be appointed Union Minister until re-elected to Parliament
eligible to be appointed Union Minister immediately after disqualification
x: Article 75(1B), inserted by the 91st Amendment, prevents a member disqualified for defection from being appointed a minister until re-elected to Parliament.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Prime Minister is the real Executive Head of the Union.
The Prime Minister can be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister is responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister is appointed by the President.
x: C is incorrect: the Prime Minister and his Council are responsible only to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)), even if he is a Rajya Sabha member. He is the real executive head, appointed by the President.

s: To what does Article 75(2), cited in accepting a Minister's resignation, relate?
o: collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
the President's pleasure regarding the tenure of Ministers
the Prime Minister's duty to furnish information
x: Article 75(2) provides that Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which operates in practice on the advice of the Prime Minister.

s: Which case held that a non-member cannot be repeatedly reappointed as a Minister without getting elected?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab
x: In S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab (2001) the Supreme Court held that the non-member provision cannot be used for repeated reappointments without election.

s: Which Article gives Ministers the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament?
x: Article 88 gives Ministers the right to speak in both Houses; 75(2) is pleasure tenure, 75(3) collective responsibility and 75(5) the six-month rule.

s: Which of the following statements regarding a Union Minister's parliamentary rights is incorrect?
o: A Union Minister can participate in joint sittings.
A Union Minister can speak and participate in the proceedings of both Houses.
A Union Minister can vote in a House of which the Minister is not a member.
A Union Minister may be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
x: C is incorrect: a Minister can speak in both Houses and joint sittings (Article 88), but can vote only in the House he belongs to.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 75(3) – Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
x: Article 75(3) makes the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; 75(2) is the President's pleasure, 75(1A) the size cap and 77(3) the business rules.

s: Which provision of the Constitution allows a person who is not a Member of Parliament to be appointed a Union Minister for a limited period?
x: Article 75(5) lets a non-member be a Minister, but he ceases to be one if he does not become an MP within six consecutive months.

s:
Assertion (A): The President of India is removed by impeachment by Parliament.
Reason (R): The impeachment procedure requires 14 days’ notice and a two-thirds majority of the total membership.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: the President is removed by impeachment under Article 61, which needs 14 days' notice and two-thirds of the total membership of each House. R only describes the procedure; it does not explain why removal is by impeachment.

s: To whom does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha address his resignation?
o: Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: Under Article 94 the Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker.

s: Who administers the Oath of Office and the Oath of Secrecy to a Union Minister?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: The President administers the oath of office and the oath of secrecy to Union Ministers, in the forms given in the Third Schedule.

s: To whom does the Governor of a State address his resignation?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Governor resigns to the President; the High Court's Chief Justice administers his oath.

s: Which of the following pairs (office – Article on its oath) is correctly matched?
x: The Vice-President's oath is in Article 69. The President's is in Article 60, the Governor's in Article 159 and Union Ministers' in Article 75(4).

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The forms of oath for the President, Vice-President and Governor are codified directly in their respective Articles.
The Governor’s oath is governed by the Third Schedule.
The Vice-President’s oath is governed by Article 69.
The President’s oath is governed by Article 60.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Governor's oath is written into Article 159 itself, like the President's (60) and Vice-President's (69). The Third Schedule holds the other oaths.

s: Under which Article do the Chief Minister and State Ministers take the oath of office and secrecy?
x: The Chief Minister and State Ministers take their oaths under Article 164(3); Article 75(4) is for Union Ministers and Article 159 for the Governor.

s: Where is the form of oath of the Vice-President laid down?
x: The oaths of the President, Vice-President and Governor are written in Articles 60, 69 and 159, not in the Third Schedule, which holds ministers' oaths.

s: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor of a State?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court concerned
The Chief Minister of the State
x: Under Article 159 the Governor takes oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State.

s: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: Under Article 60 the President takes oath before the Chief Justice of India.

s: By convention, when does the Attorney General of India resign?
o: The Chief Justice of India retires
x: The Constitution fixes no term for the Attorney General, but by convention he resigns when the government changes.

s: Which Article, among the following, specifically deals with the Attorney General's right to speak and participate in Parliament without voting rights?
x: Article 88 confers the Attorney General's right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote. Article 78 concerns the duties of the Prime Minister in relation to the President.

s: How long does the Attorney General of India hold office?
o: For a fixed term of five years
During the pleasure of the President
For a fixed term of six years
x: The Attorney General serves during the President's pleasure, so the Constitution gives him no fixed tenure.

s: Which of the following can the Attorney General of India NOT do in Parliament?
o: Vote on a motion or bill
Enjoy the privileges of an MP under Article 105(4)
Take part in the proceedings of the Houses
x: The Attorney General can speak in either House and enjoys MPs' privileges under Article 105(4), but he has no right to vote.

s: Who refers legal duties to the Attorney General of India?
x: The Attorney General performs legal duties referred by the President, not by a Governor; the State's legal adviser is the Advocate General.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor.
The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
The Solicitor General's term is fixed at appointment, usually three years.
The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
x: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet appoints the Solicitor General of India; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.

s: Under Article 177, which of the following can the Advocate General of a State NOT do?
o: Be named a member of a Legislative committee
x: Article 177 lets the Advocate General speak in both Houses and sit on committees, but he cannot vote.

s: Which restriction applies to the Attorney General of India?
o: He cannot take up private practice
He cannot advise or brief against the Government of India
He must serve as a full-time officer
He can never become a company director
x: Private practice is permitted and the office is not full-time, but the Attorney General cannot advise or brief against the Government of India; a directorship needs permission.

s: Who has been the Attorney General of India since 1 October 2022?
x: R. Venkataramani succeeded K.K. Venugopal on 1 October 2022 and was re-appointed from 1 October 2025.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the office of the Attorney General of India?
x: Article 76 provides for the Attorney General; Article 165 is for the Advocate General of a State.

s: Who among the following can be appointed Attorney General of India?
o: A person qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court
Any advocate with five years of practice
A person qualified to be a Judge of a High Court only
x: Article 76 requires the Attorney General to be qualified to be appointed a Supreme Court judge.

s: Who determines the remuneration of the Attorney General of India?
x: Under Article 76(4) the Attorney General receives such remuneration as the President determines.

s: In which courts does the Attorney General of India have the right of audience?
o: The Supreme Court and the High Courts only
All courts in the territory of India
x: In the performance of his duties the Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in India.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General of India?
o: He may take up private practice
He has the right of audience in all courts in India
He is a member of the Union Cabinet
He holds office during the pleasure of the President
x: The Attorney General is not a member of the Cabinet; he is not a full-time servant and may take private practice.

s: For how many years was R. Venkataramani re-appointed Attorney General of India from 1 October 2025?
x: R. Venkataramani, AG since October 2022, was re-appointed for two years from 1 October 2025.

s: Who was the first Attorney General of India?
x: M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India. C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Solicitor General of India – Statutory post
Advocate General of the State – Article 76
Attorney General of India – Appointed by the Chief Justice of India
x: The Solicitor General is a non-constitutional (statutory) post. The Attorney General is under Article 76 and appointed by the President; the Advocate General is under Article 165.

s: Who is the highest law officer of the Government of India?
x: The Attorney General is India's highest law officer; the Solicitor General assists the Attorney General.

s: Who was the first Solicitor General of India?
x: C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General; M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General.

s: Who appoints the Solicitor General of India?
x: The Solicitor General is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet for 3 years; the Attorney General is appointed by the President.

s: On which provision is the office of the Solicitor General of India based?
x: The Solicitor General is non-constitutional; Article 76 is the Attorney General and Article 165 the Advocate General.

s: Who is the second law officer of the Government of India?
x: The Attorney General is the first law officer and the Solicitor General, who assists him, is the second.

s: Of which system is the existence of nominal and real executives a feature?
x: Nominal and real executives and dissolution of the lower House are parliamentary features; separation of powers marks the presidential system.

s: Which one of the following is regarded as the feature that most clearly marks India as a parliamentary system?
o: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers
x: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the elected House is the characteristic feature distinguishing the parliamentary system.

s: What principally ensures the secrecy of Cabinet deliberations?
x: The oath of secrecy ensures confidentiality of Cabinet deliberations and supports the public presentation of a united government.

s: Experience under which Acts influenced India's adoption of the parliamentary form of government?
o: Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935
Regulating Act of 1773 and Pitt's India Act of 1784
x: India chose the parliamentary form because of experience under the Acts of 1919 and 1935 and to avoid a personality cult.

s: Which of the following is a necessary feature of the parliamentary form of government in India?
o: Complete separation of the executive from the legislature
x: Majority party rule, collective responsibility and the PM as the centre of power are its necessary features; complete separation of powers belongs to the presidential system.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the parliamentary form of government in India?
o: Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
Ministers being members of the legislature
Separation of powers between executive and legislature
x: Separation of powers marks the presidential system; India's parliamentary system has double membership, collective responsibility and dissolution of the LS.

s: On which model is India's parliamentary system of government based?
x: India's cabinet or responsible government follows the British Westminster model, as do Japan and Canada.

s: What does the expression 'ministers sink or swim together' mean?
o: Each minister answers only for his own department
All ministers must defend Cabinet decisions or resign
Ministers may publicly oppose Cabinet decisions
Only Cabinet Ministers share responsibility for policy
x: Collective responsibility requires all ministers to support Cabinet decisions publicly; a minister unwilling to defend such a decision must resign.

s: In which House can a no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers be moved?
o: a joint sitting of both Houses
x: Under Article 75(3) the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, so a no-confidence motion lies only there; even Rajya Sabha ministers are responsible to the Lok Sabha.

s: What is the result of the death or resignation of the Prime Minister?
o: The Council of Ministers going out of office
Automatic dissolution of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most minister automatically becoming Prime Minister
Only the Prime Minister's office falling vacant
x: The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, so his death or resignation means the Council of Ministers as a whole goes out of office.

s: Who administers the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers?
x: The President administers the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers in accordance with the Third Schedule.

s: Which Article in the States corresponds to Article 75(3) on collective responsibility?
x: Article 164(2) provides that the Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

s: Which of the following does NOT, by itself, require the whole Union ministry to resign?
o: Passage of a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha
Defeat on a money bill in the Lok Sabha
Defeat on a major policy measure in the Lok Sabha
Defeat of the Government in the Rajya Sabha
x: Only loss of Lok Sabha confidence can lead the ministry to resign; defeat in the Rajya Sabha does not by itself compel resignation.

s: Who is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary?
x: The Chief Secretary is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary. G. Sai Prasad took charge as Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary in February 2026.

s: Under whom does the Cabinet Secretariat function directly?
x: The Cabinet Secretariat, which serves the Cabinet and its committees and administers the Business Rules, functions directly under the PM.

s: Who appoints the Cabinet Secretary?
o: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
x: The ACC appoints the Cabinet Secretary, the senior-most civil servant, for two years extendable up to four.

s: Who heads the National Crisis Management Committee?
x: The Cabinet Secretary, first among equals among Secretaries and eleventh in the Table of Precedence, heads the NCMC.

s: What is the initial term of the Cabinet Secretary?
x: The ACC appoints the Cabinet Secretary for 2 years, extendable up to 4.

s: Who is the Cabinet Secretary of India who was given a one-year extension beyond 30 August 2026?
x: On 6 August 2026 Cabinet Secretary T.V. Somanathan got a one-year extension; Govind Mohan is the Home Secretary.

s: Who took charge as the Chief Secretary of Andhra Pradesh in February 2026?
x: G. Sai Prasad became AP Chief Secretary in February 2026; the Chief Secretary is the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary.

s: Who chairs the Civil Services Board at the Centre?
x: The Cabinet Secretary, the senior-most civil servant, chairs the Civil Services Board.

s: Up to what maximum total term can the tenure of the Cabinet Secretary be extended?
x: The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the ACC for 2 years, extendable up to 4 years.

s: Who is the Union Home Secretary whose tenure was extended in August 2026?
x: In August 2026 Home Secretary Govind Mohan's tenure was extended up to 22.8.2027.

s: Which body generally meets regularly and takes the policy decisions of the Union Government?
o: The Council of Ministers as a whole
x: The wider Council of Ministers (Articles 74 and 75) rarely meets as a body; the Cabinet meets regularly and takes policy decisions.

s: Which amendment inserted the word 'Cabinet' into Article 352 of the Constitution?
x: The 44th Amendment, 1978 inserted it; Article 352(3) is the only place the word 'Cabinet' appears.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Council of Ministers and the Cabinet:
1. The Council of Ministers rarely meets as a body.
2. The Cabinet directs and supervises the Council of Ministers.
3. The word 'Cabinet' appears in Article 74.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Council rarely meets as a body and the Cabinet directs it. The word 'Cabinet' appears only in Article 352(3), so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Under Article 75(2), during whose pleasure does a Union Minister hold office?
x: Article 75(2) provides that a Union Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President; in practice the Prime Minister may ask a minister to resign or advise his dismissal.

s: With whose consent may a Minister who has resigned explain his resignation in the House through a personal statement?
x: A resigned minister may make a personal statement explaining his resignation with the Speaker's consent.

s: In practice, who can ask a Union Minister to resign or advise the President to dismiss him?
x: Ministers hold office at the President's pleasure, but in practice the PM can ask a minister to resign or advise his dismissal.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 75(2) – Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
x: Article 75(2) is individual responsibility (President's pleasure); 75(3) is collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha, and 164(2) applies it to the State Assembly.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Department of Personnel?
o: It originated from the Administrative Reforms Commission of 1966.
The N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar report recommended it to provide a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform.
It was placed under the Prime Minister.
x: The Ayyangar report did not suggest a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform; the Department came in 1970 out of the 1966 ARC and was placed under the PM.

s: In which year was the N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar report on the reorganisation of the machinery of government submitted?
x: The 1949 Ayyangar report dealt with reorganising the machinery of government, including grouping of ministries and Cabinet Committees.

s: Under which of the following are Cabinet Committees in India formed?
x: Cabinet Committees are extra-constitutional bodies formed under the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961, framed under Article 77(3).

s: As of April 2025, how many Cabinet Committees function in India?
x: There are eight: Appointments, Security, Political Affairs, Economic Affairs, Parliamentary Affairs, Accommodation, Investment and Growth, and Employment and Skill Development.

s: Which of the following Cabinet Committees is NOT chaired by the Prime Minister?
x: The Accommodation Committee is chaired by a senior minister; the PM chairs the Appointments, Security and Political Affairs Committees.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Cabinet Committees?
o: The decision on caste enumeration in the Census was taken by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs is described as a 'super cabinet'.
The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs handles Centre-State and political issues.
The Committees on Investment and Growth and on Employment and Skill Development were set up in 2019.
x: Caste enumeration in the Census was decided by the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs, not the CCEA.

s: Which of the following pairs of Cabinet Committee and its concern is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Cabinet Committee on Security – Defence, national security and nuclear doctrine
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs – Economic and infrastructure projects
Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs – Senior appointments
x: Senior appointments are the concern of the Appointments Committee; the Parliamentary Affairs Committee deals with government business and parliamentary sessions.

s: Who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Accommodation (2024)?
x: Amit Shah chairs the Accommodation committee and Rajnath Singh the Parliamentary Affairs committee; these two are not chaired by the PM.

s: Which Cabinet Committee decided on caste enumeration in the Census in April 2025?
x: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs, the 'super cabinet', decided caste enumeration in the Census on 30 April 2025 – not the CCEA.

s: Who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs (2024)?
x: The Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs is chaired by Rajnath Singh; Amit Shah chairs the Committee on Accommodation.

s: Which Cabinet Committee approved the third and fourth railway lines on the Ballari-Guntakal section in July 2026?
x: The CCEA, which clears economic and infrastructure projects, approved the Rs 1,264 crore Ballari-Guntakal lines.

s: In which year were the existing Groups of Ministers (GoMs) and Empowered GoMs abolished?
x: The existing GoMs and EGoMs, criticised for delay and diluting collective responsibility, were abolished in 2014.

s: The kitchen cabinet is criticised mainly because it:
o: Is a constitutional body with a fixed membership
Is an extra-constitutional power centre that may bypass the Cabinet
Is directly answerable to the Lok Sabha
x: The kitchen cabinet is criticised as an extra-constitutional power centre because it may shape decisions while bypassing the formal Cabinet.

s: What mainly weakened Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility during 1989-2014?
o: Direct exercise of Cabinet powers by the President
Coordination committees and demands of alliance partners
Frequent dissolution of the Rajya Sabha
x: Coalition governments had to accommodate coordination committees and the demands of alliance partners, which weakened Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility.

s: What does a 'kitchen cabinet' refer to?
o: A Cabinet Committee formed under the Transaction of Business Rules
An informal inner circle of the Prime Minister's trusted colleagues and friends
The Cabinet Secretariat headed by the Cabinet Secretary
The Cabinet Ministers within the Council of Ministers
x: A kitchen cabinet is an informal inner circle of the Prime Minister's trusted colleagues and friends, including some senior ministers and non-ministers.

s: Which criticism arose from the dominance of the Union Cabinet over Parliament during single-party majority eras?
x: In single-party majority eras the Prime Minister and Cabinet generally dominated Parliament, leading to the criticism that the system resembled a 'cabinet dictatorship'.

s: With which country is the Shadow Cabinet associated?
x: The Shadow Cabinet is associated with the United Kingdom; India has no formal counterpart.

s: Which of the following can be abolished under Article 169 of the Constitution?
x: A State Legislative Council, though a permanent House, can be abolished under Article 169; the Rajya Sabha cannot be abolished.

s: By what majority must the State Assembly pass a resolution for creating or abolishing a Legislative Council under Article 169?
o: A majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
A two-thirds majority of the total membership
A simple majority of members present and voting
A majority of the total membership alone
x: The resolution must be passed by a majority of the total membership and by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.

s: What is the minimum strength of a State Legislative Council?
x: A Legislative Council must have at least 40 members and cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength.

s: Which of the following make up a bicameral State Legislature?
o: The Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council only
The Governor and the Legislative Assembly
The Governor, the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council
The Governor and the Legislative Council
x: A bicameral legislature is Governor + Assembly + Council; a unicameral one is Governor + Assembly.

s: Which State has the largest Legislative Council, with 100 seats?
x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Council, with 100 seats, among the six bicameral States.

s: How many States in India have bicameral legislatures?
x: Six States are bicameral: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh.

s: In which year was the Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh, abolished in 1985, revived?
x: The AP Legislative Council was abolished in 1985 and revived in 2007; the 2020 resolution to abolish it again was withdrawn in 2021.

s: Which Article provides for the Council of Ministers in a State?
x: Article 163 covers the State Council of Ministers; Article 74 the Union Council, Article 80 the Council of States and Articles 168, 169 and 171 the Legislative Council.

s: How is a State Legislative Council created or abolished?
o: A law of Parliament under Article 169
x: Under Article 169 Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law after an Assembly resolution; it is not an Article 368 amendment.

s: Under Article 171, what is the maximum strength of a State Legislative Council?
o: One-fourth of the strength of the Legislative Assembly
One-third of the strength of the Legislative Assembly
One-half of the strength of the Legislative Assembly
Two-thirds of the strength of the Legislative Assembly
x: Article 171 caps a Legislative Council at one-third of the Assembly's strength, with a minimum of 40.

s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh withdraw its 2020 resolution to abolish the Legislative Council?
x: The AP Assembly resolved in 2020 to abolish the Council again but withdrew the resolution in 2021.

s: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with the State Legislature?
x: Part VI, Articles 168 to 212, deals with the State Legislature.

s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Parliament of India?
x: Parliament consists of the President, the Council of States and the House of the People; State Legislative Councils are not part of it.

s: What is the name of Israel's unicameral national legislature?
x: Israel, like China, New Zealand, Sweden and Denmark, has a unicameral legislature; it is the Knesset.

s: Which Act first introduced bicameralism at the Centre in India?
x: The Government of India Act, 1919 first brought bicameralism to the Centre (Council of State and Central Legislative Assembly); the 1935 Act brought it to some provinces.

s: Which of the following is an integral part of the Parliament of India?
x: The President is an integral part of Parliament (Article 79); the Vice-President, though Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, is not a part of Parliament.

s: Which country's unicameral legislature, with 2,977 members, is the biggest Parliament?
x: China's National People's Congress, with 2,977 members, is the biggest Parliament.

s: Which Act introduced bicameral legislatures in some of the provinces?
x: The 1919 Act brought bicameralism at the Centre; the 1935 Act brought it in some provinces.

s: What is the official name of the Parliament of Russia?
x: Russia's Parliament is the Federal Assembly. The Federation Council is its upper house and the State Duma is its lower house.

s: Which is the lower House of Russia's Federal Assembly?
x: The State Duma is the lower House and the Federation Council the upper House of Russia's Federal Assembly.

s: Which is the upper House of Japan's National Diet?
x: Japan's upper House is the House of Councillors; its lower House is the House of Representatives.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Country)
A. United Kingdom
B. USA
C. Russia
D. Japan
List-II (Upper House)
1. Federation Council
2. House of Councillors
3. House of Lords
4. Senate
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: UK: House of Lords; USA: Senate; Russia: Federation Council; Japan: House of Councillors.

s: Besides its 30 elected members, how many nominated members can the Puducherry Assembly have?
x: Puducherry has 30 elected members and up to 3 nominated members; Delhi has 70 seats and Jammu and Kashmir 90 elected seats.

s: On which Article is the Legislative Assembly of Delhi based?
x: Delhi's Assembly rests on Article 239AA, inserted by the 69th Amendment (1991); Puducherry's rests on Article 239A.

s: Which Union Territories have elected members in the Rajya Sabha?
o: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
Delhi, Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli
x: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir are the three Union Territories having elected members in the Rajya Sabha.

s: The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 seeks to extend women's reservation to the legislatures of which Union Territories?
o: All Union Territories having no Legislative Assembly
Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
x: The Bill introduced in 2026 sought to extend women's reservation to the legislatures of Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir.

s: How many members does Jammu and Kashmir elect to the Rajya Sabha?
x: Only Delhi (3), Puducherry (1) and Jammu and Kashmir (4) among the UTs elect Rajya Sabha members.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 239AA, giving Delhi a Legislative Assembly?
x: The 69th Amendment (1991) added Article 239AA for the National Capital Territory of Delhi with a 70-member Assembly.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Legislature for the Union Territory of Puducherry?
x: Article 239A provides for the Puducherry Legislature; Article 239AA is for Delhi.

s: How many elected members does the Legislative Assembly of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir have under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019?
x: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 provides an Assembly of 90 elected members for the UT of Jammu and Kashmir.

s: How many seats does the Legislative Assembly of Delhi have?
x: The Delhi Assembly, based on Article 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991), has 70 seats.

s: How many members does Delhi elect to the Rajya Sabha?
x: Delhi elects 3 members to the Rajya Sabha, Puducherry 1 and Jammu and Kashmir 4.

s: Which of the following is cited as an argument against a second chamber?
o: It gives a second examination to every Bill
It brings in experts through nomination
x: Delay and duplication are cited against a second chamber; a double check, regional representation and expert nomination are arguments in its favour.

s: To whom is the criticism of a second chamber, 'If it agrees it is superfluous, if it dissents it is mischievous', attributed?
x: This criticism of a second chamber is attributed to Abbé Sieyès.

s: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar defended the Rajya Sabha mainly as a forum for what?
o: Dignified debate and delaying hasty legislation
x: Ayyangar regarded the Rajya Sabha as a forum for dignified debate that could delay legislation passed in the passion of the moment.

s:
Consider the following statements about the second chamber:
1. Abbé Sieyès called it superfluous if it agrees and mischievous if it dissents.
2. N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar defended the Rajya Sabha as a House of dignified debate.
3. A second chamber speeds up law-making.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A second chamber causes delay and duplication; it does not speed up law-making.

s: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
x: A Money Bill must be returned within 14 days, showing the Rajya Sabha is weaker than the Lok Sabha in financial matters.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Rajya Sabha can initiate a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers.
The Speaker certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
The Speaker presides over a joint sitting of Parliament.
The Rajya Sabha has no vote on Demands for Grants.
x: A no-confidence motion is a device of the Lok Sabha alone, not the Rajya Sabha.

s: Which Schedule of the Constitution gives the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to the States?
x: Rajya Sabha seats are allotted by population in the Fourth Schedule, unlike the equal representation in the US Senate.

s: How is each state represented in the US Senate?
x: The US Senate gives equal representation – 2 per state (100 in all) – and has no nominated members.

s: Comparing the Rajya Sabha and the US Senate, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Rajya Sabha – election by elected MLAs through PR-STV
x: The US Senate has no nominated members; the Rajya Sabha has 12.

s: Under which Schedule are seats in the Rajya Sabha allotted to the States?
x: Seats are allotted by population under the Fourth Schedule (Arts. 4 and 80(2)), not equally as in the US Senate; UP has the most (31).

s: Which one of the following groups consists only of States having one seat each in the Rajya Sabha?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur and Tripura
x: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura each have one Rajya Sabha seat. The group in option a contains only such States.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Telangana have?
x: Telangana has 17 Lok Sabha seats; Andhra Pradesh has 25 and Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir 5 each.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Tripura have?
x: Tripura has 2 Lok Sabha seats (and one Rajya Sabha seat); Sikkim, Mizoram and Nagaland have one Lok Sabha seat each.

s: The Andhra State Act of 1953 and the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act of 2014 were enacted under which Article of the Constitution?
x: Both the creation of Andhra State in 1953 and the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014 were carried out under Article 3, which concerns the formation and alteration of States.

s: How many Rajya Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 11 Rajya Sabha seats; Telangana has 7, Uttarakhand 3 and Tripura 1.

s: Which State has 12 seats in the Rajya Sabha?
x: Karnataka has 12 Rajya Sabha seats, followed by Gujarat 11, Odisha 10 and Kerala 9.

s: How were undivided Andhra Pradesh's 18 Rajya Sabha seats split after 2014?
x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended the Fourth Schedule: AP got 11 and Telangana 7 Rajya Sabha seats.

s: How many seats does Andhra Pradesh have in its Legislative Assembly?
x: Andhra Pradesh has a 175-member Assembly, 25 Lok Sabha and 11 Rajya Sabha seats; Telangana's Assembly has 119.

s: Which of the following pairs (State – Rajya Sabha seats) is correctly matched?
x: West Bengal and Bihar have 16 each; Maharashtra has 19, Tamil Nadu 18 and Uttar Pradesh 31.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 25 Lok Sabha seats, 11 Rajya Sabha seats and 175 Assembly seats.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh has 25 seats in the Lok Sabha and 11 in the Rajya Sabha.
2. Telangana has 17 seats in the Lok Sabha and 7 in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP has 25 LS and 11 RS seats; Telangana has 17 LS and 7 RS seats.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Maharashtra have?
x: Maharashtra has 48 Lok Sabha seats (and 19 in the Rajya Sabha).

s: In the Rajya Sabha polls of 18 June 2026 for 24 seats in 10 States, how many seats were from Andhra Pradesh?
x: Of the 24 Rajya Sabha seats polled on 18 June 2026, 4 were from Andhra Pradesh.

s: Who elect the representatives of a State in the Rajya Sabha?
o: all members of the State Legislative Assembly, including nominated members
the elected members of the State Legislative Assembly
the elected members of both Houses of the State Legislature
the people of the State directly
x: Under Article 80(4) they are elected by the elected MLAs through PR-STV; nominated MLAs do not take part.

s: In the present Rajya Sabha of 245 members, how many seats represent the Union Territories?
x: The present Rajya Sabha has 225 representatives of States, 8 of Union Territories and 12 nominated members.

s: In which election can nominated members of the Rajya Sabha vote?
o: both the President and the Vice-President
neither the President nor the Vice-President
x: Nominated members vote in the Vice-Presidential election but not in the Presidential election.

s: In which year was Sachin Tendulkar nominated to the Rajya Sabha?
x: Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012 and Mary Kom in 2016.

s: Which of the following is NOT a field listed in Article 80(3) for nomination to the Rajya Sabha?
x: Article 80(3) lists literature, science, art and social service; sports is not among them.

s: Which Union Territories are represented in the Rajya Sabha?
x: Among the Union Territories only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have Rajya Sabha seats.

s: Who was the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1952)?
x: Rukmini Devi Arundale was the first nominated woman (1952); Nargis Dutt was the first film actress nominee (1980).

s: A nominated member of the Rajya Sabha may join a political party within what period of taking his seat without disqualification?
x: A nominated member may join a party within 6 months; after that he is disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.

s: How are members of the Rajya Sabha from the States elected?
o: Single transferable vote by all MLAs and MLCs
Majority vote of the Lok Sabha
Single transferable vote by elected MLAs
x: Under Article 80(4) elected MLAs choose Rajya Sabha members by PR-STV; nominated MLAs and MLCs cannot vote.

s: Which sportsperson was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 2016?
x: Mary Kom was nominated in 2016 and Sachin Tendulkar in 2012, though sport is not a field listed in Article 80(3).

s: On whose advice does the President dissolve the Lok Sabha before its term?
x: Early dissolution is on the PM's advice, not the Speaker's, and cannot be challenged in court; the five-year term runs from the first meeting (Art. 83(2)).

s: The term of a member of the Rajya Sabha is six years. By which of the following is this term fixed?
o: Rules of Procedure of the Rajya Sabha
x: The six-year term of a Rajya Sabha member is fixed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and not directly by the Constitution.

s: In the first Rajya Sabha constituted in 1952, how were the members who were to retire first selected?
o: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: To initiate the one-third retirement cycle, the terms of the initial members were curtailed and the members retiring first were decided by lottery.

s: Which Lok Sabha was extended during the National Emergency of 1975–1977?
x: The Fifth Lok Sabha, constituted for the period 1971–1977, was extended during the 1975–1977 Emergency.

s: During a National Emergency, an extension of the Lok Sabha cannot continue beyond how long after the Emergency ends?
x: The term can be extended by law one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ends.

s: Which of the following Lok Sabhas was NOT dissolved before completing its term?
x: The 4th, 6th, 9th, 11th, 12th and 13th Lok Sabhas were dissolved early; the 14th is not among them.

s: For how long does a member elected to a casual vacancy in the Rajya Sabha serve?
o: The rest of the predecessor's term
x: A casual vacancy in the Rajya Sabha is filled for the remainder of the term only.

s: In which year was the 12th Lok Sabha constituted?
x: The 12th Lok Sabha was constituted on 10 March 1998 after the February-March 1998 elections and was dissolved on 26 April 1999.

s: What fraction of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every second year?
x: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House; about one-third of its members retire every second year.

s: On which date was the First Lok Sabha constituted after the first general elections?
x: The first Lok Sabha was duly constituted on 17 April 1952 after the general elections of 1951-52.

s: In which year did the First Lok Sabha hold its first sitting?
x: The members of the first Lok Sabha met for the first time on 13 May 1952.

s: How is the present strength of the Lok Sabha made up?
o: 530 members from States and 13 from Union Territories
524 members from States and 19 from Union Territories
525 members from States and 18 from Union Territories
x: The present strength is 543, comprising 524 members from the States and 19 from the Union Territories.

s: What was the elected strength of the First Lok Sabha?
x: The First Lok Sabha had 489 elected seats; the present elected strength is 543.

s: Till which year did the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 extend the reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs?
x: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST reservation by ten years, till 2030, and ended only the nomination of Anglo-Indians.

s: Which Article provides for elections on the basis of universal adult suffrage?
x: Adult suffrage is under Article 326; Article 84(b) deals with Lok Sabha membership.

s: For how long was the reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs initially provided?
x: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to their population; the reservation was first given for ten years.

s: At what number did the 7th Amendment, 1956 fix the strength of the Lok Sabha?
x: The 7th Amendment, 1956 fixed the Lok Sabha at 520; the 31st Amendment, 1973 raised it from 525 to 545.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the strength of the Lok Sabha?
o: The First Lok Sabha had 489 elected seats.
x: 552 was the old maximum that counted 2 Anglo-Indian nominees; the present maximum is 550.

s: What are the maximum and present strengths of the Lok Sabha?
x: The constitutional maximum is 550, while the present strength is 543. The older figure of 552 included two nominated Anglo-Indian members.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha?
x: The 104th Amendment (in force from 25 January 2020) ended Anglo-Indian nomination and extended SC/ST reservation till 2030.

s: Under which Article could the President nominate two members of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha?
x: Article 331 allowed the President to nominate two Anglo-Indians; Article 333 dealt with nomination to State Assemblies.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the President as a component of Parliament?
o: The President is a part of Parliament but not a member of either House.
No Bill passed by Parliament becomes law without the President's assent.
The President summons and prorogues the Houses of Parliament.
The President sits in Parliament as a member while addressing the Houses.
x: The President is a component of Parliament but never sits as a member of either House.

s: Under Article 87, at the commencement of which sessions does the President make a special address to both Houses?
o: the first session after each general election and the first session of each year
only the first session after each general election
only the first session of each year
x: The Article 87 special address is made at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year; Article 86 is the general power to address either or both Houses.

s: Which Article deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha?
x: Article 81 covers the Lok Sabha; 79 the constitution of Parliament, 80 the Rajya Sabha and 83 the duration of the Houses.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 81 – Duration of Houses of Parliament
Article 83 – Reservation of seats for SCs and STs
Article 330 – Composition of the Lok Sabha
Article 84 – Qualification for membership of Parliament
x: Article 84 deals with qualifications for membership. Article 81 is composition, Article 83 duration and Article 330 SC/ST reservation.

s: Which Article provides for the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
x: Article 89(2) provides for the Deputy Chairman, chosen from among Rajya Sabha members; the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman under Articles 64 and 89(1), and Article 93 is the Lok Sabha Speaker.

s: Which Article of the Constitution defines a Money Bill?
x: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; Article 109 lays down the special procedure for it. Article 108 is joint sitting, 111 assent to Bills and 117 Financial Bills.

s: To which of the following is the constitutional position of the Indian President in relation to Parliament most closely comparable?
o: The Governor of a State in relation to its Legislative Assembly only
The President of France in relation to its Senate
The President of the United States in relation to Congress
The Crown-in-Parliament in the United Kingdom
x: The inclusion of the President as a component of Parliament resembles the Crown-in-Parliament principle in the United Kingdom. It differs from the United States, where the President is separate from Congress.

s: Which veto does the President use when he returns a Bill once to Parliament for reconsideration?
x: Returning a Bill once is the suspensive veto; keeping it pending is the pocket veto and withholding assent is the absolute veto.

s: Which Article deals with Appropriation Bills?
x: Article 114 covers Appropriation Bills; 100 is voting and quorum, 105 privileges and 113 the procedure for estimates.

s: Under Article 123, when can the President promulgate an Ordinance?
o: A National Emergency is in operation
The Rajya Sabha rejects a Bill
x: The President issues Ordinances under Article 123 only when Parliament (either House) is not in session.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Article 112 deals with the Annual Financial Statement; Article 93 is the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, and Article 108 the joint sitting.

s: In which Part of the Constitution do Articles 79 to 122 occur?
x: Parliamentary provisions in Articles 79 to 122 are contained in Part V of the Constitution.

s: Under which Article may the President address either House or both Houses together at any time?
x: Article 86 lets the President address either or both Houses; Article 87 is the special address at the first session.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the duration of the Houses of Parliament?
x: Article 83 gives the Lok Sabha a five-year term and makes the Rajya Sabha a permanent House.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?
x: Article 80 deals with the Council of States (Rajya Sabha); Article 81 with the Lok Sabha.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
x: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting of the two Houses.

s: Under Article 79, what is the position of the President with respect to Parliament?
o: An integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House
A member of the Rajya Sabha
A member of the Lok Sabha
x: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses; the President is an integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House.

s: If the two Houses of Parliament disagree on a constitutional amendment bill, which one of the following is the consequence?
o: The bill fails because no joint sitting is permitted for such a bill.
The Lok Sabha may pass the bill by a simple majority in a second sitting.
The Supreme Court decides which version of the bill shall prevail.
The President convenes a joint sitting under Article 108.
x: There is no provision for a joint sitting in respect of a constitutional amendment bill. Failure to secure the required approval in either House causes the bill to fall.

s: Without whose approval can no tax be imposed?
x: No tax can be levied without Lok Sabha approval; questions and motions are other tools of control over the executive.

s: In the case of which Bills are the powers of the Rajya Sabha restricted?
x: The Rajya Sabha has equal powers on Constitutional Amendment Bills and can introduce Ordinary and Amendment Bills; it is restricted only for Money Bills.

s: Which of the following is correct about a Financial Bill of category I?
o: Can be introduced in either House of Parliament
Can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and both Houses have equal powers in its passage
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days
x: A Financial Bill of category I can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, but unlike a Money Bill both Houses have equal powers in its passage.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Demands for grants — Rajya Sabha may vote on them
Money Bill — Rajya Sabha to return it within fourteen days
Joint sitting — Presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: The Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants. A Money Bill is returned within fourteen days, a joint sitting is presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker, and a no-confidence motion is moved in the Lok Sabha.

s: On which of the following matters do the two Houses of Parliament NOT have equal powers?
o: Passing a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency
Approval of an Ordinance promulgated by the President
Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court
x: Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency; the Houses are equal on the other three.

s: Which one of the following matters is within the equal powers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
o: Initiation of a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers
Consideration of the report of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
x: Both Houses have equal powers in considering the reports of the CAG, UPSC and Finance Commission. The other matters are associated with the superiority of the Lok Sabha.

s: In the Budget process, which of the following can the Rajya Sabha NOT do?
o: Make recommendations on a Money Bill
x: The Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants, which is a Lok Sabha power.

s: Which of the following can be done only by the Lok Sabha?
x: Only the Lok Sabha can discontinue a National Emergency; both Houses approve emergencies and take part in impeachment and removal of judges.

s: If the Rajya Sabha approves a National Emergency while the Lok Sabha is dissolved, within how many days of its first sitting must the new Lok Sabha approve it?
x: The Rajya Sabha may approve the proclamation for the time being; the newly constituted Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.

s: Under which Article can the Rajya Sabha authorise the creation of new All-India Services?
x: Article 312 covers new All-India Services; 249 deals with State List legislation in the national interest and 67(b) with initiating the Vice-President's removal.

s: By what majority must a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 be supported?
o: a simple majority of members present and voting
two-thirds of members present and voting
a majority of the total membership
x: It needs two-thirds of members present and voting, is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time.

s: Under which Article can a proceeding to remove the Vice-President be started only in the Rajya Sabha?
x: Under Article 67(b) a resolution to remove the Vice-President can begin only in the Rajya Sabha.

s: For how long does a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 remain in force?
o: Until the Lok Sabha is dissolved
x: An Article 249 resolution is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time.

s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 authorises which body to make laws on a State List subject?
x: Article 249 empowers Parliament, not State Assemblies, to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest.

s: What is the minimum age for membership of the Rajya Sabha?
x: The minimum age is 30 for the Rajya Sabha and 25 for the Lok Sabha; no educational qualification is prescribed.

s: What is the minimum age for membership of the Lok Sabha?
x: A Lok Sabha member must be at least 25 years old; for the Rajya Sabha the minimum is 30 years.

s: Which of the following minimum age requirements is NOT correct?
o: Prime Minister or Chief Minister – 25 years
x: The Governor's minimum age is 35 years, not 30 (Article 157). The President and Vice-President need 35, and a PM or CM from the lower House 25.

s: Which Article lays down the minimum age qualification for the Governor of a State?
x: Article 157 covers the Governor; 58(1)(b) the President, 66(3)(b) the Vice-President and 84(b) members of Parliament.

s: Under Article 243F(1)(a), what is the minimum age to contest Panchayat elections?
x: Article 243F(1)(a) prescribes 21 years for Panchayat membership, while Article 326 fixes the voting age at 18.

s: Which of the following pairs (office – minimum age) is correctly matched?
o: Prime Minister or Chief Minister – 25 years
x: A Prime Minister or Chief Minister from the lower House needs 25 years. The correct ages are 21 for a municipal member, 30 for the Rajya Sabha and 35 for the Vice-President.

s: In which year did the 61st Amendment, which lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years, come into effect?
x: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age to 18, and it took effect in 1989.

s: In which case (2006) did the Supreme Court uphold the open ballot and the removal of the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha elections?
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Sita Soren v. Union of India
Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
x: Kuldip Nayar (2006) upheld both the removal of the domicile requirement and the open-ballot system.

s: Before whom does a Member of Parliament make the oath or affirmation before taking his seat?
o: The President or a person appointed by him
The Election Commission or a person authorised by it
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha only
x: Under Article 84, a candidate for Parliament must make an oath or affirmation, in the Third Schedule form, before a person authorised by the Election Commission.

s: Which of the following pairs about qualifications for Parliament is correctly matched?
o: Domicile in the State for Rajya Sabha candidates – still required
Domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha – never existed
Candidate for Parliament – registered elector in a parliamentary constituency
Candidate for Parliament – elector only in the State he resides in
x: A parliamentary candidate must be a registered elector in a parliamentary constituency; the Rajya Sabha domicile requirement existed but was removed in 2003.

s: To which offices does the highest minimum entry age in the Constitution, 35 years, apply?
